list.name: asset_id
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT asset_id FROM assets ORDER BY asset_id

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM gateways WHERE status = 'ONLINE'

panels.title: Temperature Stream by Device

targets.rawSql: SELECT bucket_ts AS "time", asset_id AS metric, val_double AS "value" FROM telemetry_gapfill($__timeFrom(), $__timeTo(), INTERVAL '5 minutes', ARRAY[${asset_id:sqlstring}]::text[], ARRAY['Systems/TEMPERATURE']) ORDER BY asset_id, bucket_ts

panels.description: Reads the five-minute rollup, not the raw hypertable. The average is derived from the stored sum and count -- the rollups keep those rather than an average precisely so that coarser buckets can be combined without weighting a minute with two samples the same as a minute with two hundred. min_double/max_double are available on the same rows if the excursion matters more than the mean.

panels.title: Status Timeline by Device

targets.rawSql: SELECT bucket_ts AS "time", asset_id AS metric, val_string AS "value" FROM telemetry_gapfill($__timeFrom(), $__timeTo(), INTERVAL '5 minutes', ARRAY[${asset_id:sqlstring}]::text[], ARRAY['Controller/EXECUTION']) ORDER BY asset_id, bucket_ts

panels.description: Reads the five-minute rollup. A state cannot be averaged, so the rollup carries last_string -- the value the metric held at the end of the bucket -- which is the correct summary for Controller/EXECUTION.

panels.title: Latest Telemetry Readings

targets.rawSql: SELECT time, asset_id, metric_name, COALESCE(val_double::text, val_string, val_bool::text) AS value FROM telemetry_latest WHERE asset_id IN (${asset_id:sqlstring}) ORDER BY asset_id, metric_name

panels.description: Reads the telemetry_latest view, which performs the DISTINCT ON once, on this server, against the (asset_id, metric_name, time DESC) index. Its cost is bounded by how many series exist rather than by how much history does.

targets.rawSql: SELECT ac.asset_id, a.asset_name, ac.metric_name, COALESCE(ac.val_double::text, ac.val_string, ac.val_bool::text) AS value, ac.updated_at FROM asset_config ac JOIN assets a ON a.asset_id = ac.asset_id WHERE ac.asset_id IN (${asset_id:sqlstring}) ORDER BY ac.asset_id, ac.metric_name

panels.title: Shared Buffer Hit Ratio
panels.description: Share of relation reads served from shared_buffers rather than the OS/disk, from pg_stat_io (PostgreSQL 16+). Cumulative since the last stats reset, not a rate. A sustained fall means the working set has outgrown shared_buffers.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100.0 * sum(hits) / NULLIF(sum(hits) + sum(reads), 0), 2) AS "hit_ratio" FROM pg_stat_io WHERE object = 'relation' AND context = 'normal'

panels.title: Blocks Read From Disk
panels.description: Relation blocks pg_stat_io reports as physically read. Counts every backend type, so it includes autovacuum and TimescaleDB background workers as well as queries.

targets.rawSql: SELECT sum(reads) AS "reads" FROM pg_stat_io WHERE object = 'relation'

panels.title: Requested Checkpoints
panels.description: Checkpoints forced by WAL volume rather than by time, from pg_stat_checkpointer (PostgreSQL 17+). THIS IS THE NUMBER TO WATCH: timed checkpoints are the healthy path, and a requested count climbing beside them means max_wal_size is too small for the write rate, so the historian is checkpointing on ingest bursts instead of on a schedule.

panels.title: Avg Checkpoint Write Time
panels.description: Mean time spent writing buffers per checkpoint. Rising alongside Requested Checkpoints is the signature of checkpoint pressure; rising alone usually means slower storage.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(write_time::numeric / NULLIF(num_timed + num_requested, 0), 1) AS "avg_write_ms" FROM pg_stat_checkpointer

panels.title: I/O by Backend Type and Context
panels.description: The pg_stat_io breakdown behind the tiles above. `context` separates ordinary access (normal) from bulk paths (vacuum, bulkread, bulkwrite), which is what distinguishes a dashboard query missing cache from a retention job scanning chunks. Cumulative since stats_reset.

targets.rawSql: SELECT backend_type AS "Backend", context AS "Context", hits AS "Cache hits", reads AS "Disk reads", CASE WHEN coalesce(hits,0) + coalesce(reads,0) > 0 THEN round(100.0 * hits / (hits + reads), 1) END AS "Hit %", writes AS "Writes", extends AS "Extends", evictions AS "Evictions", fsyncs AS "Fsyncs" FROM pg_stat_io WHERE object = 'relation' AND (coalesce(hits,0) > 0 OR coalesce(reads,0) > 0 OR coalesce(writes,0) > 0) ORDER BY coalesce(hits,0) + coalesce(reads,0) DESC
